Gross domestic product per head at curre.label: Gross domestic product per head at current market prices
Gross domestic product per head at curre.subtitle: GDP per head including the effects of inflation
Gross domestic product per head at curre.longDescription: This indicator shows gross domestic product (GDP) per head at current market prices in pounds, in the UK, for 1998 to 2024.
Gross domestic product per head at curre.caveats:
Notice (September 2026) - The Regional Accounts team identified an issue in the process used to convert from the old International Territorial Level (ITL) 2 subregions to the new subregions introduced in the ITL25 update. The issue affects ITL2 subregions K5 (West of England), K6 (North Somerset, Somerset and Dorset), K7 (Gloucestershire and Wiltshire), L3 (North Wales), L4 (Mid and South West Wales), L5 (South East Wales), M2 (Highlands and Islands), and M3 (West Central Scotland). All lower-level areas within these subregions are also affected, as are any city and enterprise regions containing parts of these subregions. ITL1 countries and regions are unaffected. Any estimates for these areas have been suppressed to avoid releasing potentially misleading information. The team expect to release a complete dataset within four to six weeks which will then be updated on Explore Local Statistics shortly after.

This time series includes the effects of inflation and is most useful for comparison of levels between different areas.

2024 data are provisional.

Data for the City of London has been excluded from the line chart and bar chart on this service due to its very high GDP figures and very low population, which distort the overall representation. Please refer to the accompanying dataset below or the [data source](https://www.ons.gov.uk/economy/grossdomesticproductgdp/bulletins/regionaleconomicactivitybygrossdomesticproductuk/previousreleases) for this information.

While GDP per head can be a useful way of comparing regions of different size, comparisons can be affected by commuting flows into or out of the region. Therefore, these [figures should be used with caution](https://blog.ons.gov.uk/2018/11/23/mind-the-gap-why-the-uk-might-not-be-the-most-regionally-unequal-country/). For such areas, it is advisable to refer to GVA per hour worked or GVA per job filled for a direct measure of economic performance.

Gross domestic product per head in chain.label: Gross domestic product per head in chained volume measures
Gross domestic product per head in chain.subtitle: GDP per head with the effects of inflation removed by considering changes in quantity between consecutive periods, holding prices from previous periods constant
Gross domestic product per head in chain.longDescription: This indicator shows gross domestic product (GDP) per head in chained volume measures (CVM) in 2023 money value, in pounds, in the UK, for 1998 to 2024.
Gross domestic product per head in chain.caveats:

The team expect to release a complete dataset within four to six weeks which will then be updated on Explore Local Statistics shortly after.

This time series has the effects of inflation removed by considering changes in quantity between consecutive periods, holding prices from previous periods constant and is most useful for monitoring growth over time within any given area.

2024 data are provisional.
